title: The Principle of Complementarity in Quantum Theory
text:
Quantum mechanics suggests that particles, such as photons, exhibit wave-particle duality, meaning they manifest both as discrete particles and as extended waves depending on the experimental setup. This concept is not a contradiction but rather a fundamental property of matter at microscopic scales.

The principle of complementarity states that certain pairs of properties—like position and momentum, or wave nature and particle nature—are mutually exclusive yet both necessary for a complete description of reality. The act of measurement fundamentally influences the outcome, forcing the system into one observable state while obscuring others.

Understanding this duality requires abandoning classical intuitions about objective reality. The observed properties are context-dependent, emphasizing that physical knowledge is always limited by the methods used to acquire it.
